- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid premature mean reversion.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior period), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast increase to 2–5% for next period.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive drops >5%), model often fails to recognize; reduce forecast slope by 10–20%.
- If model forecast is rising steadily but true outcome shows volatility or divergence, reduce forecast slope by 1–3% to account for sentiment-driven noise.
- For periods with sentiment history including 0.5 or 0.25, model tends to overreact; apply a 2–5% downward bias to forecast if sentiment is not confirmed.
- If true outcome is below model by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, model may be overconfident; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly but true outcome shows strong upward momentum, reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid lagging.
